Record date: 2129-05-08
South Elizabeth Seychelles Hospital INTERNAL MEDICINE DEPARTMENT Location: 4923 Olivia Parkway Suite 217, Lake Jennabury
PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 80 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 05/08/29 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Increased shortness of breath, persistent edema, and worsening anxiety.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax presents for follow-up approximately two weeks after his last visit. He reports a notable deterioration in his respiratory status, characterized by increased shortness of breath at rest and during minimal exertion. He describes episodes of orthopnea, requiring him to sleep propped up with multiple pillows. The bilateral lower extremity edema persists, with his shoes feeling increasingly tight; he notes a further weight gain of 3 pounds since his last visit, totaling a 10-pound increase over the past month.
Mr. Fairfax continues to utilize his nebulizer and albuterol inhaler excessively, now averaging twelve uses of the inhaler daily. He reports that his wheezing has intensified, and he experiences increased fatigue and a sense of impending doom, which has exacerbated his anxiety levels. Sleep remains elusive, averaging only 2-3 hours per night, despite his efforts to engage in relaxation exercises.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + weight gain, + fatigue, no fevers or chills. Pulmonary - + shortness of breath at rest, + nocturnal wheezing, + productive cough with yellowish sputum, - hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain or palpitations, + orthopnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - + joint pain, + persistent bilateral lower extremity edema. Neurological - + increased anxiety, + insomnia, no dizziness or headaches.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) 2. Hypertension 3. Osteoarthritis 4. Persistent fatigue 5. Anxiety and depression (ongoing management)
PAST SURGICAL HISTORY
1. Right knee arthroscopy in 2018.
FAMILY HISTORY
Father - history of lung cancer. Mother - history of hypertension.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives alone in , . Former carpenter, now retired. Quit smoking 15 years ago. Occasional alcohol use. No illicit drug use.
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
MEDICATIONS ON FOLLOW-UP
1. Albuterol inhaler as needed, currently using twelve times daily. 2. Lisinopril 20 mg daily. 3. Fluticasone/salmeterol 500/50 MDI, 2 puffs twice daily. 4. Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaler, 2 puffs daily. 5. Acetaminophen 500 mg as needed for pain. 6. Furosemide 80 mg twice daily (ongoing). 7. Sertraline 200 mg daily. 8. Prednisone 40 mg daily for COPD exacerbation (completed course).
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: T 98.7F, HR 85, BP 142/90, RR 30, O2 sat 70% on room air.
General: Elderly male in moderate to severe respiratory distress, appears fatigued and anxious. HEENT: No nasal congestion, oropharynx clear. Pulmonary: Diminished breath sounds bilaterally, marked wheezing noted on expiration, significant rhonchi present. Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs. Extremities: 4+ pitting edema in bilateral lower extremities, no erythema or warmth.
LABORATORY DATA
1. CBC: WBC 10.2, Hgb 9.5, Hct 27.5, Plt 215. 2. BMP: Na 128, K 4.3, Cl 92, CO2 18, BUN 70, Cr 4.2, Glucose 85. 3. BNP: 1200 (further elevated). 4. Thyroid function tests: TSH 3.2 (within normal limits).
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. COPD management: Mr. Fairfax's respiratory condition has significantly worsened, necessitating immediate intervention. A referral to pulmonary medicine is critical for evaluation of potential non-invasive ventilation support and further management of his COPD exacerbation. 2. Hypertension and renal function: The worsening renal function, indicated by elevated creatinine levels, raises concerns for acute kidney injury, potentially secondary to diuretic therapy. A nephrology consultation is urgently requested to reassess renal function and to optimize diuretic therapy. 3. Lower extremity edema: The persistent and worsening edema remains a significant concern. Furosemide will be increased to 100 mg twice daily, with close monitoring of weight and renal function. Dietary sodium restrictions will be reinforced, and Mr. Fairfax will be educated on signs of fluid overload. 4. Mental health: Mr. Fairfax's anxiety and insomnia persist, warranting a more aggressive approach. A psychiatry referral will be expedited for medication management, and continuation of cognitive-behavioral therapy will be strongly encouraged.
Patient education was reinforced regarding the importance of recognizing exacerbation signs, adherence to medication, and lifestyle modifications to manage COPD and edema effectively.
